text:
reena: Quick bug report from a user: the API reference shows `max_new_tokens` in the OpenAPI example but our Python SDK sample uses `max_tokens`. Folks are getting surprising truncation.

theo: Oh right. Historically we accepted both names at the server level, but that caused ambiguity with some tokenizers. We standardized on `max_new_tokens` for generation endpoints to avoid mixing with upstream token count semantics.

akash: I can update the Python example and the curl snippet. Proposal: canonicalize examples to `max_new_tokens` everywhere in the API reference, and add a tiny compatibility note `# legacy: max_tokens -> max_new_tokens` with a one-line mapping.

reena: Please also update the OpenAPI example so auto-generated SDK snippets remain consistent. We should add a short migration note in the docs page: "If you previously used `max_tokens`, rename to `max_new_tokens` for generation endpoints." Link to the migration guide.

akash: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4589 - changes: OpenAPI examples, curl/py/js snippets, and an examples/compatibility.md entry. I also added a unit check for the examples runner so we fail if examples use deprecated params.

docs-bot: CI: docs build passed for PR #4589 ✅ preview: https://deploy-preview-4589--docs.redwood.ai/api-reference/generate

piyu: Another related note: response schema docs list `choices` as an object in one place, and `outputs` in another. We should pick a single canonical response shape. Recommendation: keep `choices` (array) with fields `{ index, text?, delta? }` and deprecate `outputs` alias. Add both a non-streaming sample and a streaming sample showing `choices[].delta`.

theo: Agreed. I'll update the OpenAPI response schema and add the two examples. Also include a short paragraph about streaming vs non-streaming finalization (i.e., final chunk may have `text` while interim chunks use `delta`).

reena: Cool. After merge I'll add a brief line to the release notes and the migration guide. Thanks all :thumbsup:
